semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: Clinical neurophysiology often involves the measurement and study of electrical properties of the nervous system, closely aligning with electrophysiology.

parent_domains.justification: Neuroscience is the broader domain that encompasses clinical neurophysiology as it covers the comprehensive study of the nervous system.

closest_parent_domain.justification: Being the overarching field that includes clinical neurophysiology, neuroscience is the closest parent domain.

child_domains.justification: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a specific area within clinical neurophysiology focused on the recording of electrical activity in the brain.

closest_child_domain.justification: EEG directly deals with brain electricity, making it the closest specific domain under clinical neurophysiology.

sibling_domains.justification: Neuroanatomy, like clinical neurophysiology, is a specialized study within the larger field of neuroscience.
Cognitive neuroscience, like clinical neurophysiology, is an area within the broader neuroscience field.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Cognitive neuroscience is often intertwined with neurophysiological studies in understanding brain function relating to cognition.

unrelated_domains.justification: Neurotopology deals with the topological aspects of neural structures, which are not directly related to clinical neurophysiology.
Physiological psychology focuses on the physiological mechanisms underlying psychological processes, which may not align directly with the focus of clinical neurophysiology.
While related to the brain, neuropsychiatry focuses on psychiatric conditions, which may not always involve neurophysiological methods.
Visual neuroscience focuses specifically on the visual processing system, rather than the broader scope of clinical neurophysiology.
Neuropsychology focuses on the relationship between brain function and behavior, distinct from the clinical measurements in neurophysiology.
Computational neuroscience focuses on the theoretical modeling of brain function, which may not directly overlap with practical measurements in clinical neurophysiology.
